caption: You’ll want to watch to the end
video_overlay_text_observed: Screen-recorded clips played in sequence (BBC broadcast footage, an interview with Netanyahu, a rabbi speaking); narrator speaks over them. No burned-in caption track.
audio_content_summary: Montage arguing 9/11 foreknowledge: the 2001 BBC World broadcast announcing the Salomon Brothers Building (WTC 7) collapse while the building still stands behind correspondent Jane Standley; Netanyahu describing his 1995 book as having predicted militant Islam bringing down the World Trade Center; and an unnamed rabbi's account of a "two big buildings in the land of Edom" prophecy and of a rabbi who prayed near the towers and said "say bye-bye to those buildings."
implied_frame: Framing: the buildings' fall was known in advance. Verified here: the BBC broadcast happened and pre-dated the collapse by more than twenty minutes; Netanyahu did say the book predicted it, and the book's actual sentence is a different one. Not asserted here: that either fact establishes foreknowledge, that WTC 7 was brought down deliberately, that the "Edom" passage refers to the Twin Towers, or the unnamed-rabbi anecdote, for which no primary trace was found.
capture_method: Pristine original media + metadata pulled from Instagram's CDN via yt-dlp; delivery webm derived once (VP9 video copied, audio normalized to -16 LUFS / -1.5 dBTP off the source AAC — no re-recording, no in-place re-encode).
